To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BEN is a useful marker of the developing inner ear and that BEN expression in the inner ear is regulated in response to noise exposure.

BEN expression defines a single sensory-competent zone from which all the sensory organs develop in the chick inner ear; and that the regenerating hair and support cells do not express this molecule, which highlights a molecular difference between development and regeneration.
BEN expression is detected in the developing inner ear from stage 11 and that BEN expression levels are high in the prosensory patch.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the development of the vertebrate ear.
understanding the mechanisms of development and regeneration of the auditory system in the chick.
the molecular basis of hair cell development in the inner ear and the molecular mechanisms of hair cell regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BEN is a cell adhesion molecule expressed in sensory epithelia of the inner ear, and that it plays an important role in the development of sensory organs.
the BEN gene expression is a marker of sensory organ development and is involved in the development of the sensory epithelia.
the BEN protein is a useful marker of sensory cell differentiation in the inner ear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BEN expression defines the sensory region in the developing inner ear, but is lost in the adult inner ear.
BEN is expressed in the prosensory region of the inner ear and is upregulated in response to damage, but is not expressed in regenerating hair cells.
BEN is a cell adhesion molecule that is expressed in the prosensory patch of the developing inner ear and in regenerating hair cells of the posthatching inner ear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BEN expression in the inner ear is restricted to a single region, which is the sensory competent zone of the inner ear.
the BEN gene is expressed in the developing inner ear in the same region where hair cells develop and in a pattern that is similar to the pattern of the hair cells.
BEN expression in the inner ear is a marker for sensory competence and that BEN expression in response to noise exposure is not a marker for regeneration.
